'''Muneer Ahmad Rashid''', [[Fellow of the Pakistan Academy of Sciences|FPAS]] (born 1934), also spelled as '''Munir Ahmad Rashid''', is a Pakistani [[Mathematical physics|mathematical physicist]] and emeritus [[professor]] of [[Applied mathematics|applied]] and [[mathematical physics]] at the Centre for Advanced Mathematics and Physics of the [[National University of Sciences and Technology, Pakistan|National University of Sciences and Technology]].

A physicist turned mathematician, Rashid has made numerous contributions in [[Special unitary group]], [[applied mathematics]], [[Theoretical physics|theoretical]] and [[nuclear physics]], [[Rotation (mathematics)|SO(2)]], and [[dark energy]]. He was a student of physicist and scientist [[Abdus Salam]].

==Education==
Rashid was born in [[Lahore]], British India where he had completed his high-school from there in 1950. Rashid attended the [[University of the Punjab|Punjab University]] in 1950, and had received his double [[Bachelor of Science|BSc (Hons)]] in [[physics]] and [[mathematics]] in 1955.<ref>{{Cite web| title =About Symposium-CCIS: Prof. Dr. Munir Rasheed| website =Technomoot| url =http://technomoot.edu.pk/CCIS/About.aspx| format =(html)| url-status =dead| archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20100601070847/http://technomoot.edu.pk/CCIS/About.aspx| archive-date =1 June 2010}}</ref> In 1957, he did his [[Master of Arts|M.A.]] in mathematics and taught as a lecturer in mathematics at the [[Government College University, Lahore|Government College University]] where he stayed there until 1960. Rashid then travelled to United Kingdom in 1961 to attend [[Imperial College London]].

During the 1960s, an physicist Salam was also teaching at Imperial College London where he was supervising the doctorate studies of my many Pakistani students. Rashid joined the Salam's group and began working with Salam's group at the Imperial College. In 1964, Munir Ahmad did his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in [[Mathematical physics]] under the supervision of Salam, where his [[doctoral thesis]] were entitled "''Generalization of Mass Formula in [[Unitary symmetry|Unitary Symmetries]]''".<ref>{{Cite web
  | title =Generalization of Mass Formula in Unitary Symmetries
  | publisher =American Physical Society
  | year =1963
  | url =http://publish.aps.org/search/field/author/Rashid_Muneer_Ahmad
  | format =(Html)
  | access-date =22 September 2010 }}</ref> Munir Rashid also did his [[Doctor of Science|D.Sc.]] in mathematical physics under the supervision of Salam at the [[University of London]] in 1980.<ref>{{Cite web| last =HEC| first =Higher Education Commission| title =Muneer Ahmad Rashid| url =http://sc.hec.gov.pk/aphds/submit.asp?supid=1775| url-status =dead| archive-url =https://archive.today/20121228095739/http://sc.hec.gov.pk/aphds/submit.asp?supid=1775| archive-date =28 December 2012}}</ref>

==Academic career==
Rashid, following his doctorate degree, came back to Pakistan where he joined [[Quaid-i-Azam University]] as an [[associate professor]] in 1968. In September 1968, he travelled to United States where he joined [[University of Rochester]]<ref>{{Cite web| title=Official Bulletin of the University of Rochester/1968-69 | url=https://rbscp.lib.rochester.edu/sites/default/files/atoms/files/1968-69_UR_Bulletin.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190302102402/https://rbscp.lib.rochester.edu/sites/default/files/atoms/files/1968-69_UR_Bulletin.pdf | archive-date=2019-03-02}}</ref> as a Visiting Senior Research Associate. Rashid stayed in United States until 1970 and, during this time, he had carried out the research in mathematical physics. In 1970, Rashid came back to Pakistan and re-joined Quaid-i-Azam University as a professor.

During the 1960s, Rashid had closely worked with Salam's students to the field of [[SU(3)]] or [[Special unitary group]]. Rashid had closely worked with an Israeli theoretical physicist [[Harry J. Lipkin]], who is also a student of Salam. During the 1960s, Lipkin was working on SU(3) field and had brought his work to Salam to re-check the work, which according to Lipkin, his predictions did not meet the results as new experimental results from were available to them from [[CERN]].<ref>{{Cite web
  | title =Response to the Award of the Wegner Medal: See Unitary Symmetry 
  | url =http://www.ph.utexas.edu/~bohmwww/wigner2002/lipkinresp.pdf  
  }}</ref> Salam travelled back to Pakistan next day and on Salam's recommendation, Lipkin met with Rashid in London. Rashid gained famed when he had independently discovered the error in Lipkin and Salam's work. Imperial College's Physics Department head, Gerry Brown, who was an editor-in-chief, of ''Physics Letter'', accepted the suggestion from Imperial College that Salam's and Rashid's names to be list of authors. The next day, the paper appeared as ''Unitary Symmetry: A collaboration of three Israelis and two Pakistanis''<ref>{{Cite web   | last = Lipkin    | first =Harry J.    | author-link =Harry J. Lipkin    | title =Response to the Award of the Wegner Medal: See Unitary Symmetry     | year =2002    | url =http://www.ph.utexas.edu/~bohmwww/wigner2002/lipkinresp.pdf}}.</ref> Rashid continued his close association with Salam in PAEC where he had worked on the mathematics problems related to the science of the designing of nuclear weapons. He played a major role in the development of the designing of the atomic bomb, through his calculations on critical mass theory. Rashid had contributed in [[scattering theory]] where he had solved the mathematics problems in scattering theory, mainly predicting the scattering of optical waves and the behaviour of the elementary particles in the general process of [[Nuclear testing|testing]] of the [[nuclear device]].<ref>{{Cite journal
  | last =Rashid
  | first =Muneer Ahmad
  | title =Scattering by a Potential with r-2n tail in the Born Approximation
  | journal =The Journal of Chemical Physics
  | volume =60
  | pages =3729–3790
  | year =1974
  | issue =9
 | doi =10.1063/1.1681608
 | bibcode =1974JChPh..60.3729R
 }}</ref> Rashid also had applied the [[Quantum harmonic oscillator#Hamiltonian and energy eigenstates|Hamiltonian harmonic oscillator]] theory to approximate the optical wavelengths and the transition amplitudes of the [[Quantum particle]]s in the tested nuclear device.<ref>{{Cite journal
  | last =Rashid
  | first =Muneer Ahmad
 |author2=[[Ghulam Murtaza (physicist)|Ghulam Murtaza]] |author3=H.U.Rahman
  | title =Non-Linear waves in a two-component hot nuclear plasma
  | journal =Journal of Physics
  | volume =10
  | pages =1249–1257
  | year =1974
}}</ref> To approximate the data and the position of the nuclear particles and their effect in an affected nuclear test sites, Rashid used complex [[mathematical series]], [[Integral]]s and mathematical [[permutation]] where he published his work under the supervision of Salam at the PAEC.<ref>{{Cite journal
  | last =Rashid
  | first =Muneer Ahmad
  | title =The mathematical series and number of permutations on n symbols which contain at least one cycle of length = I
  | journal =Journal of Mathematics
  | volume =07
  | pages =35–47
  | year =1974
  }}</ref>

==Research work==
Specialized in mathematical physics under Salam, Rashid had developed an early interest in scattering theory where he had published numerous papers. His contribution to scattering theory at [[Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission]] had made breaking discoveries to the field of nuclear physics. On 29 March 2009, at the Mathematical conference, Rashid, using the resources and work of [[Richard Taylor (mathematician)|Richard Taylor]] and [[Andrew Wiles]], proved the [[Fermat's Last Theorem]], and the papers containing the published proof of Fermat's Last Theorem were presented at the conference.<ref>{{Cite web| title =One Day Mathematical Conference in Honour of Professor Muneer Ahmad Rashid| url =http://camp.nust.edu.pk/conferences/oneday/index.php| url-status =dead| archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20110813025735/http://camp.nust.edu.pk/conferences/oneday/index.php| archive-date =13 August 2011}}</ref> On 1 April 2006, at the 12th Regional Conference on Mathematical Physics, held by the [[National Center for Physics]], Rashid proof and presented his papers on "''Transition amplitude for time-dependent linear harmonic oscillator with Linear time-dependent terms added to the Hamiltonian''" where he had proposed and solved mathematical problems on [[Hamiltonian matrix]] [[Spherical harmonics|Spherical]] and [[Cylindrical harmonics]] by applying the [[Hamiltonian mechanics]].<ref>{{Cite web
  | last =Rashid
  | first =M. Ahmad
  | title =Transition amplitude for time-dependent linear harmonic oscillator with Linear time-dependent terms added to the Hamiltonian
  | website =Munir Ahmad Rashid
  | publisher =M. A. Rashid
  | year =2006
  | url =http://www.ncp.edu.pk/docs/12th_rgdocs/Munir-Rasheed.pdf
  }}</ref> He also made numerous contribution on [[pure mathematics]], [[Statistical mechanics]] and [[Statistical physics|physics]].
